name: Context-linked modal entry, exit and focus continuation
summary: For a genuinely modal task, purposeful naming, keyboard entry/exit, context-sensitive first focus and logical post-close focus are treated as related lifecycle decisions rather than automatic library guarantees.
problem: A dialog can visually isolate a task while keyboard focus cannot reach its content, leave it, follow meaningful order or resume the interrupted workflow intelligibly.
context: A deliberately modal confirmation/short task with a known invoking element, task consequences and a defined close/continue pathway, including cases where the invoker disappears.
observed_solution: APG documents titled modal with focus moved inside, Tab wrap, Escape and conditional initial/return focus; WHATWG documents conditional native dialog focus and inertness algorithms; WCAG requires keyboard functionality/exit, meaningful applicable focus order and visible focus; USWDS and Primer describe name, close and focus-ref conventions whose application-level effectiveness must be tested.
rationale: WCAG O01–O04 (here O01,O02,O03,O04) establish criterion-specific obligations, not APG Escape or an arbitrary focus hook. APG O13–O16 describe illustrative modal interaction and legitimate exceptions; WHATWG O08/O09 apply only to native modalities; USWDS O21/O22 and Primer Product O26 provide product conventions; pinned Primer O31/O32 reveal JSX/callback/ref wiring only. C1 C01/C02/C04/C05/C06/C07/C08/C13/C20 retain authority splits, forced action, conditional descriptions and uninspected imported hooks. No app runtime or AT behavior is established.
tradeoffs: Containment can preserve context during a true modal interaction yet becomes harmful if users lack an available keyboard-only exit or a task-compliant action path.
First focus may need static structured content, the least destructive action or a likely next step; selecting a universal first button can displace meaningful content or amplify risk.
Returning focus to the opener is common guidance, but opener deletion or workflow advancement may require a different logical destination.
Implementing predictable focus and dismissal requires task-state reasoning and later tests; a library's documented refs/callbacks alone are insufficient.
applicability: Genuinely modal tasks whose surroundings are intentionally unavailable until a user-controlled exit or completion path.
Dialogs with lengthy semantic content, irreversible actions, invokers that may unmount, or meaningful subsequent workflow targets requiring context-sensitive focus.
Modal implementations that claim aria-modal and thus require verification that the outside is actually unavailable.
non_applicability: Nonmodal disclosure, tooltips, native popover modes or generic floating layers are not required to implement modal Tab wrapping or background inertness.
Required acknowledgment variants may legitimately differ from APG default Escape/close control; they still require explicit review of the applicable keyboard exit obligations and user choices.
No universal initial-focus target, close key, automatic returnFocusRef success, or specific native/React dialog API is adopted.
accessibility_implications: For the rendered app, separately test keyboard-only exit under WCAG 2.1.2, focus order under 2.4.3 where applicable, focus visibility under 2.4.7, and focus-not-entirely-obscured under 2.4.11; no criterion automatically mandates APG's exact component API.

APG's aria-modal label is not a behavioral guarantee; verify genuine outside interaction isolation before claiming it. In complex text, aria-describedby may be omitted where APG advises preserving structure.
Pinned O31 leaves a possible aria-describedby target gap when default subtitle is omitted, but source-level suspicion is NOT a demonstrated browser/AT failure.
performance_implications: No measured performance cost for focus management, scroll locking, Portals, stacking or handler subscriptions; results UNKNOWN.
responsive_implications: On narrow/zoomed layouts, check initial-focus scrolling, visible focus, action reachability and obscuration in the concrete app; no responsive or mobile validation ran.
implementation_notes: C1 C01/C02 distinguishes keyboard-exit WCAG obligations from APG modal pattern Escape and USWDS bounded forced-action exceptions; do not silently choose a universal close policy.
WHATWG O08/O09 apply to native dialog algorithms only; source code O31/O32 is pinned primer/react@7f5303d803986887187d86dcebaeda22a4dc6823, with hook implementation outside authorized source read.
Primer Product docs unpinned/rights UNKNOWN; pinned implementation is the same publisher, not corroborating independent votes.
USWDS publisher WCAG 2.1 AA component-check summaries and Primer authored test assertions O33 do not establish Kirion runtime pass.
Review opener-missing and meaningful task continuation cases (APG O16); prevent auto-promoting an unconditional return-focus claim.

counterexamples.summary: APG recommends a static first-focus target for complex/scrolling content instead of invariably selecting the first interactive control.
counterexamples.context: Dialog containing multiple paragraphs or semantic structures where focusing a lower button would scroll the beginning away.

counterexamples.summary: Post-close focus may go to a newly relevant workflow item when the invoking control no longer exists.
counterexamples.context: Add-row workflow where dialog completion creates a new row or removes opener.

counterexamples.summary: USWDS forced-action gate intentionally differs from an ordinary dismissible dialog.
counterexamples.context: A task-authorized required acknowledgment with explicit choice pathways; keyboard exit still needs separate conformance review.
